what: GATX leases railcars. It owns a fleet of tank cars, hoppers and freight wagons and rents them to shippers on multi-year leases, in North America, Europe and India. It also owns a joint venture leasing aircraft engines.
customers: Chemical producers, refiners, agricultural shippers, mining companies and industrial manufacturers who need railcars but do not want to own them, plus airlines leasing engines through the Rolls-Royce joint venture.
money: Leasing tank cars and freight cars to North American shippers, plus maintenance services.
Railcar leasing in Europe and India.
Share of the aircraft spare engine leasing joint venture and portfolio management.
moat: Railcars last forty to fifty years and cost a great deal upfront, which is exactly why shippers prefer to lease. GATX has over a century of experience in asset residual values and maintains its own repair network. New railcar building capacity in North America is limited, so the existing fleet holds value, and tank car regulations make older cars scarce.
risks: Debt of about $12.7B against a $6.5B market value is enormous, though normal for a leasing company whose assets are financed.
Lease rates depend on railcar supply and on freight volumes, both cyclical, and residual values can fall if a car type goes out of favour.
Rising interest rates raise the cost of financing a leasing fleet, which compresses the spread between lease income and funding cost.
Only three analysts cover the stock, so the $219.00 average target rests on very few views.
The shares trade at about 18.4 times EV/EBITDA, which is not obviously cheap for a leasing business.
opportunities: Revenue has grown every year shown, from $1.3B in 2021 to $1.7B in 2025, and free cash flow of $863.8M is very large relative to the market value.
Railcar lease rates have been strong because the North American fleet has shrunk and new build capacity is limited.
The aircraft engine leasing joint venture benefits from record aircraft utilisation and a shortage of spare engines.
GATX has paid a dividend without interruption for over a century, which reflects the predictability of long-term lease income.
watch: Lease renewal rates. A leasing company's earnings are decided by whether expiring leases renew above or below their old rate, and GATX reports that figure directly.
